strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps on register-saturated low-occupancy kernels regresses
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with varying num_warps configs to a kernel that is already register-saturated (156+ registers/thread) and occupancy-limited caused registers/thread to jump from 156 to 255 and achieved occupancy to drop from 6.25% to 3.12%, nearly doubling kernel duration (47 µs → 84 µs). When a kernel is already bottlenecked by register pressure and shared memory bank conflicts, autotuning num_warps alone does not address the root cause and can force the compiler to spill more registers or choose worse configurations, further degrading occupancy. The actual plan intent (enabling TF32 via ALLOW_TF32=True) was not reflected in the diff — the diff only added autotune configs without changing ALLOW_TF32, so the intended optimization was never applied.
applicable_when: Never applicable as a standalone fix when the kernel is register-saturated and the root cause is a constexpr flag (e.g. ALLOW_TF32=False) that forces scalar FP32 instead of Tensor Core MMA.
do_not_apply_when: Do not add @triton.autotune with only num_warps/num_stages variation when: (1) registers/thread > 128 and occupancy < 10%, (2) the primary bottleneck is a constexpr flag controlling compute path (scalar vs tensor core), (3) the grid is already smaller than SM count (waves_per_sm < 0.5). In these cases, fix the root cause (e.g. ALLOW_TF32=True) before or instead of autotuning.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune with key=[] means autotuning runs once but still compiles multiple configs. When registers/thread is near the hardware maximum (255), reducing num_warps (e.g. from 4 to 2) halves the block size and can cause the compiler to allocate even more registers per thread due to reduced register sharing, worsening occupancy. The intended fix (ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = False → True) was never applied in the actual diff despite being the stated plan.

applicable_when: The B matrix has layout [K=256, N=128] with stride_bk=1 (K-contiguous) and stride_bn=256 (N-stride=256 elements). Inside the K-loop, the load `B + b_k_idx_vals + 256 * offs_b_n[None, :]` accesses B[k, n] where consecutive threads in the warp step along the N-dimension with stride 256. Since 256 % 32 == 0, every thread in a warp maps to the same shared memory bank, producing the observed 8-way bank conflict. NCU confirms 3,526,656 bank conflicts = 66% of all shared wavefronts. The fix is to stage B tiles through explicitly allocated shared memory with a +8-element padding on the N-dimension (BLOCK_N+8 columns), so that consecutive K-rows land on different banks. This is a purely structural change — the mathematical values loaded and the accumulation are identical — so correctness is preserved. Previous attempts that changed the index formula caused correctness failures (items 88d48c1d, 4de93ebe); padding avoids any index rewrite. The CPIStall (45.8% of cycles stalled on MIO/shared memory) confirms shared memory latency is the dominant stall reason.
